_comment: Surface biomes and how they lie across the width. climate: the width runs cold (x = 0) to hot; orders are the ways the biomes can lie along it, one picked per world, each one naming every enabled biome once. share = [lo, hi] fraction of the width, drawn per world and normalised; no biome ends below min_share. seam = how far a border's skin and rock interleave, ramp = how far its height profile blends, both as a fraction of the width clamped to tiles. Rows: top, soil, stone are tile names, soil_wall and stone_wall wall names (stone reaches from the soil to a little under the surface band). soil_depth = [lo, hi] tiles. snow: top turns to this tile above a fraction of the surface band. map_color: tools/worldmap.gd. height: base = lift as a fraction of the surface band; big, mid, fine scale the world's noise (1 = the old meadow); ridge = sharp peaks, dune = short swells, both 0-1; step = most tiles between neighbouring columns (a Medium steps up 1 and jumps 6).

orders.name: meltwater
orders.doc: Cold woods, the range, its melt pooling in the fens below, then grass drying out into desert.

orders.name: rain_shadow
orders.doc: Cold woods running down to fens and grass, and a range that keeps the rain from the desert behind it.
